text: dsh-prompt-predict 是面向 DSH 网页客户端的输入框提示词联想插件。助手回复结束后，它根据当前会话调用会话模型，生成下一条可直接发送的建议，并以灰色 ghost text 显示在输入框附近。用户可按 Tab 采纳、按 Esc 忽略，也能重新生成或切换候选。设置页可配置启用状态、模型、建议语言、上下文范围、长度和历史记录，用户覆盖项保存在本机。适合希望更快续写对话、获得后续提问建议的 DSH 用户；预测使用所选模型。

dsh-prompt-predict adds next-message suggestions to the DSH web composer. After an assistant reply, it uses the conversation and selected model to show a draft as gray ghost text. Tab accepts it, Esc dismisses it, A settings page controls language, context, length, and history.
想让 DSH 在助手回答后，顺手给我一条可以接着发的消息。
有没有办法在输入框里预览下一句，按 Tab 就能直接采用？
我常常不知道接下来该问什么，能不能根据当前对话给点提示？
希望模型回复结束后自动准备一个简短的后续问题。
DSH 的对话输入框能显示灰色的续写建议吗？
我想切换不同的下一句候选，而不是每次都从头想。
Can DSH suggest a useful follow-up message after the assistant finishes?
I want to preview a draft in the composer and accept it with Tab.
dsh-prompt-predict 的功能「预测下一条消息」：助手回复完成后，插件把当前会话交给所选模型，生成一条符合对话语言的后续消息，并在输入框显示为灰色 ghost text。
dsh-prompt-predict 的功能「采纳或忽略建议」：建议显示时按 Tab 可将文本插入 DSH 输入框，Esc 可收起建议；用户开始输入或已有草稿时不会覆盖草稿。
dsh-prompt-predict 的功能「重新生成候选」：用户可请求生成新建议，并在候选间切换；插件会限制切换次数并避免近似重复。
dsh-prompt-predict 的功能「配置预测行为」：设置页允许启停预测、选择模型和建议语言，并调整上下文、输出长度、历史记录等参数；用户覆盖项保存在本机配置文件。

Codex-style composer predictions for DeepSeek Harness
After each reply, your next prompt is ghosted right into the composer — Tab to accept, Esc to dismiss, start typing and it's gone

🌏 中文 · English

dsh-prompt-predict README · dsh-prompt-predict：`dsh-prompt-predict` is a [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/) plugin: after every assistant turn it predicts **the message you are most likely to type next** and floats it into the composer as gray ghost text. The suggestion never enters the editor — only pressing `Tab` inserts it, and even then it stays undoable — so a wrong prediction costs you nothing.

dsh-prompt-predict README · ✨ Features：- **Single-line or multi-line** — sentences stay one line; code snippets, lists and multi-paragraph replies keep their line breaks and indentation
- **A suggestion the moment a reply ends** — gray ghost text rendered at the composer's first character, matching the editor's caret position, font size and line height
- **Three interactions** — `Tab` to accept, `↻` (or `↓`) for a different suggestion, `Esc` to dismiss; typing hides it, and clearing the draft brings it back
- **Lightweight context** — only the most recent user/assistant *text*; tool results, attachments and system prompts never leave your machine
- **Follows the current session model by default** — nothing is hard-coded to a provider, the prediction call reuses whatever model the session itself uses; you can also pin a cheaper model
- **No repeats, no dead ends** — a repeat of the previous suggestion triggers an automatic "give me a different one"; a reasoning level the real model doesn't support falls back automatically, so you never hit "settings look fine but no suggestion ever appears"
- **Everything is adjustable** — on/off, provider / model, response timeout, context size and
dsh-prompt-predict README · 🚀 Installation：The plugin is published on npm. Options are ordered by convenience.

dsh-prompt-predict README · Install inside DSH (recommended)：**GUI**: open the plugins page → **Add plugin** → enter the package name `dsh-prompt-predict` → install.

**Or the dsh CLI** — pin any published version with pnpm's `@version` syntax:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-prompt-predict@0.2.13
```

Replace `--profile` with your own profile (usually `desktop` on the desktop app, `web` for the web build), then **restart DSH**.

**Upgrade to the latest release**

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-prompt-predict@latest
```

dsh-prompt-predict README · Install inside DSH (recommended)：From a source checkout, `bash scripts/update.sh [profile]` does the same and also converges the lockfile; it refuses to run while the app is still up — quit it first. The settings page has a **Check for updates** button next to the version and also checks npm automatically when opened (at most once every 10 minutes). When a newer version exists it links straight to **DSH sidebar → Plugins → Installed plugins → dsh-prompt-predict → Versions → Update**, where DSH handles the download, rollback and restart; a copyable CLI command remains as a fallback. Update notices live only in Settings — there is no banner under the composer.

dsh-prompt-predict README · Install inside DSH (recommended)：> ⚠️ **The CLI only installs the package.** DSH loads a plugin only when it is also listed in
> `dsh.profile.bundles` inside `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`. Verified: with the package
> installed but not in that list, the plugin's routes answer `404` and nothing loads. The GUI route
> above handles it for you; with the CLI add `"dsh-prompt-predict"` to that array yourself, or just
> run `scripts/install.sh` below, which does both steps.
dsh-prompt-predict README · Install inside DSH (recommended)：> You'll find the switch and all parameters under **Settings → Prompt Suggestions**.

dsh-prompt-predict README · Install from a release tarball：Every [release](https://github.com/ferrisching/dsh-prompt-predict/releases) carries the exact
tarball that is on npm (`shasum` matches the registry), which is handy for offline machines or for
pinning an artifact you can verify:

```bash
gh release download v0.2.13 --repo ferrisching/dsh-prompt-predict --pattern '*.tgz'
dsh plugin --profile desktop add ./dsh-prompt-predict-0.2.13.tgz
```

dsh-prompt-predict README · Install from a release tarball：Same caveat as the CLI route above: add `"dsh-prompt-predict"` to `dsh.profile.bundles` yourself,
or run `scripts/install.sh` instead.

dsh-prompt-predict README · Install from source：```bash
git clone https://github.com/ferrisching/dsh-prompt-predict.git
cd dsh-prompt-predict
bash scripts/install.sh

dsh-prompt-predict README · make sure the app is fully quit first (Cmd+Q) — the script refuses to run while it is up：```

The script packs this repo on the fly, installs it into the profile's `node_modules`, and adds `dsh-prompt-predict` to `dsh.profile.bundles`. The default target is `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop`; for another profile:

```bash

dsh-prompt-predict README · Requirements：- Verified on **DSH `0.2.1-rc.3`** (web build; the desktop app runs the same host and client code)
- `node` / `pnpm`: the install script prefers DSH's own runtime under `~/.dsh/dsh-runtimes/*/dependencies` and only falls back to `PATH`
- macOS / Linux; Windows untested

dsh-prompt-predict README · ⌨️ Usage：1. Chat normally, wait for the assistant to finish its turn, and leave the **composer empty**
2. About 350 ms later a gray suggestion appears, with `Tab` / `↻` / `Esc` on its right
3. Pick what you need:

dsh-prompt-predict README · ⌨️ Usage：| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| `Tab` | Accept the whole thing while the composer is focused (only now is it inserted, and it stays undoable) |
| `↻` (button on the right) | **Reroll** — ask the model for a different suggestion |
| `↓` | Generate the next suggestion (counts toward *Max switches*); if this round already has later suggestions, move forward through them for free. With no suggestion showing and an empty composer it fetches one immediately. `Ctrl/⌘+↓` works as a fallback |
| `↑` | Return to the previous suggestion in this round (free) |
| `Ctrl/⌘+Shift+Space` | Trigger a prediction by hand; rerolls when one is already showing |
| `Esc` | Dismiss this one |
| Just start typing | It disappears; **clearing the draft brings it back** (only `Esc` is a permanent dismissal) |
dsh-prompt-predict README · ⌨️ Usage：Suggestions only appear when the composer is empty and the session isn't running. Switching sessions or interrupting a reply clears any pending suggestion.

dsh-prompt-predict README · ⚙️ Settings：| Setting | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Enable predictions | Master switch | On |
| Provider / model | Model used for the prediction call; pick "Follow current session model" to reuse the session's own model | Follow current session model |
| Response timeout (advanced) | 1–60 seconds | 12 seconds |
| Context size (advanced) | Small 3 / Standard 8 / Large 12 messages | Standard 8 |
| Context budget (advanced) | Character cap sent to the helper call, 1000–20000 | 6000 |
| Output length | How long a suggestion should be, in **characters** (20–400) — no token maths. Pinning a Latin-script language also shows the equivalent in words; CJK stays in characters because word segmentation is undefined there. The host derives a generous token safety cap from it (per language) and writes the character budget into the prompt; a reply that still gets cut is retried with more room and marked **cut off · raise the output length** | 120 |
| Keep multi-line formatting | Allow code snippets/lists to keep line breaks and indentation (off = always one line) | On |
| Switchable suggestions | When on, ↓ generates the next suggestion and ↑ returns to the

dsh-prompt-predict README · ⚙️ Settings：The bottom of the settings page shows a **recent predictions** list (default 10, adjustable): time, session, model, latency, and whether the reasoning level was auto-downgraded, a reroll happened, the suggestion was truncated by the output cap, or the call failed (with the reason). The list stays folded to the newest run (`▸ Show all` opens the rest), the newest run's suggestion text is expanded by default, and clicking a row's `▸` expands that run's text while collapsing the previous one. Records live in the app's own local storage (the Electron renderer's storage on desktop, the page's `localStorage` on web) and are never uploaded. No more guessing why nothing appeared.

dsh-prompt-predict README · ⚙️ Settings：- Changes take effect **immediately** — no DSH restart
- Settings are stored at `~/.dsh/dsh-prompt-predict/config.json` (mode 600)
- Precedence: **user-saved settings > cordis patch deploy defaults > built-in defaults**

dsh-prompt-predict README · 🔌 HTTP API：The plugin registers a same-origin prefix route `/dsh-prompt-predict` on DSH's web server; both the settings page and the composer suggestion go through it. Every endpoint is authenticated with DSH's browser cookie (`connection.requestRejection`) — off-machine callers get 401/403.

dsh-prompt-predict README · 🔌 HTTP API：| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/dsh-prompt-predict/status` | Current session model, effective settings, saved overrides, deploy defaults |
| GET | `/dsh-prompt-predict/catalog` | All providers and models (for the dropdowns) |
| GET | `/dsh-prompt-predict/efforts?provider=&model=` | The reasoning levels that model actually supports |
| POST | `/dsh-prompt-predict/settings` | Save settings; `{ "reset": true }` restores defaults |
| POST | `/dsh-prompt-predict/suggest` | `{ sessionId }` → one suggestion |

dsh-prompt-predict README · 🔌 HTTP API：Every endpoint accepts an optional **`x-dsh-locale`** header (`zh` / `en`, default Chinese) deciding which language validation errors and prediction failures come back in. The client sends the active UI language automatically.

dsh-prompt-predict README · 🧩 How it works：1. `lib/index.js` is the plugin entry point and registers the same-origin HTTP route
2. On `suggest`, `lib/predict.mjs` trims the session down to the most recent user/assistant plain text — walking backwards under both a message-count limit and a character budget
3. That trimmed history is **framed as a single request-only user input** before it reaches the helper model: DSH assistant messages must carry a full `stream` / `replayState`, so a trimmed fragment cannot masquerade as one (same approach session-title uses)
4. The streamed reply is normalized (code fences, `Suggestion:` prefixes and wrapping quotes stripped, newlines collapsed) and returned to the client

dsh-prompt-predict README · 🧩 How it works：For model selection, `provider` / `model` set to `auto` means "follow the session": no route is hard-coded onto the helper call, and `predictNextPrompt` inherits whatever the session itself selected.

**Client side** (`client/`)

- Injects into the `conversation.composer.dock` (lifecycle mount point next to the composer) and `settings.section` slots
- The ghost text is an **overlay** — it is never written into the Lexical editor; only accepting goes through `inputActions.insertText`

dsh-prompt-predict README · Client source layout：The client is built from ordered fragments in `client/src/` (`npm run build:client` writes `client/client.js`). DSH loads exactly one client script, so the split is a source-organisation aid, not native ES modules; `pretest` and `prepack` rebuild automatically.

dsh-prompt-predict README · Real-DSH smoke test (macOS, optional)：`npm run test:smoke` boots a disposable DSH profile, installs this repo as a local tarball, starts a local mock LLM and drives a headless Edge via CDP. It checks that: a real reply produces a ghost, `Tab` is ignored while another input is focused, `Tab` accepts inside the composer, reroll changes the suggestion, and pause hides/restores it. Requires the DeepSeek Harness app and Microsoft Edge; override paths with `DSH_SMOKE_DSH` and `DSH_SMOKE_EDGE`. It is deliberately not part of `npm test`.

dsh-prompt-predict README · 🛠️ Development：```bash
git clone https://github.com/ferrisching/dsh-prompt-predict.git
cd dsh-prompt-predict
npm test        # 71 cases: 51 host-side + 20 client render smoke tests
```

```
.
├── lib/                 Host side (plain ESM, no build step)
│   ├── index.js         Plugin entry point, registers the HTTP route
│   ├── host-route.mjs   Same-origin API: status / catalog / efforts / settings / suggest

dsh-prompt-predict README · 🛠️ Development：> `test/client-render.mjs` is the only automated safety net for the client side: no browser needed — a tiny React stand-in expands the components into a plain object tree so the test can assert that the ghost shows up and that `Tab` / `↻` / `Esc` are all there. It exists because of a real incident: the overlay referenced a variable it never read from props, the render threw, React's error boundary swallowed it, and the symptom was "the API returns a suggestion but nothing ever appears" — while every host-side test was green.
dsh-prompt-predict README · 🛠️ Development：The tests need no DSH runtime: a fake ctx plus a local HTTP server cover route registration, settings validation, route inheritance and end-to-end calls.

dsh-prompt-predict README · 🔐 Security and cost：- **One** small helper call per assistant turn by default; an extra attempt only happens when the reply hits the length limit, the reasoning level needs downgrading, or a suggestion needs rerolling — **four calls is the hard ceiling** (primary, reasoning-level fallback, length retry, reroll), and they share a single timeout budget
- Suggestions are **not written to the session log**; only after you accept with `Tab` and send does the text become a real message
- Only trimmed user/assistant plain text is sent — tool results, attachments and system prompts never leave the machine
- Both the settings page and the suggestion endpoint sit behind DSH's own browser-cookie authentication

dsh-prompt-predict README · 🩺 Troubleshooting：**No suggestion appears at all**

- It runs only after an assistant turn ends (about 350 ms later), never while the reply is still streaming.
- The composer must be empty. If you already have a draft, the prediction is skipped on purpose — no call is made.
- A brand-new session with no messages has nothing to predict from.
- Check Settings → Prompt suggestions: *Enable predictions* must be on, the session must not be paused, and **Recent predictions** must not show an error.
dsh-prompt-predict README · 🩺 Troubleshooting：**"Prediction failed: …" shows under the composer** (it appears after two failures in a row)

dsh-prompt-predict README · 🩺 Troubleshooting：| Reason text | What to do |
|---|---|
| `Request timed out` | Raise *Response timeout* in Advanced |
| `Provider "…" is unavailable` / `has no model "…"` | Pin a provider and model instead of following the session model |
| `Prompt prediction is turned off` | Turn the switch back on |
| anything else | Open Settings → Prompt suggestions → **Recent predictions**; the row carries the host's exact reason |

**Suggestions come in the wrong language**

dsh-prompt-predict README · 🩺 Troubleshooting：- `Auto` (the default) detects the language from your recent messages by majority vote over the last five, so a message that is mostly a pasted log can skew it.
- Pin one instead: Settings → *Suggestion language* (with a *Region* picker for Chinese, English, Portuguese, Spanish, French, German and Dutch).
- The UI language does **not** affect the suggestion language — those are two separate settings.

**A suggestion ends with "cut off · raise the output length"**

dsh-prompt-predict README · 🩺 Troubleshooting：- Raise *Output length*. A capped reply is already retried once with more room before the marker appears.
- Reasoning models can spend a large part of the budget before writing any text; if this happens often, raise the length or keep *Reasoning effort* off (the default).

**Tab does nothing**

dsh-prompt-predict README · 🩺 Troubleshooting：- `Tab` is intercepted only while a suggestion is visible; with no ghost it behaves normally.
- Click into the composer first — the overlay is positioned over the editor's caret box, and `Tab` acts on the focused editor.

**Ghost text sits on top of what I typed**

- Fixed in `0.2.7`: it hides on paste, IME composition and drag-and-drop, and it no longer appears while the composer has a draft. Upgrade if you still see this.

**"Recent predictions" is empty**

dsh-prompt-predict README · 🩺 Troubleshooting：- Records are local to the app's own storage, are wiped by the *Clear* button, and runs recorded before `0.2.5` carry no suggestion text.

**I upgraded but nothing changed**

- Host-side changes (settings fields, prompt construction) apply after **restarting the app**; client-side changes apply after **reloading the window**. The version label in `package.json` is not rewritten by a window reload.

dsh-prompt-predict README · ⚠️ Known limitations：- Verified only on DSH `0.2.1-rc.3`; other versions untested
- Depends on the host's `conversation.composer.dock` and `settings.section` slot names — a major DSH update may require adapting
- Predictions consume quota on the selected model; pinning a fast small model is cheaper than following a reasoning model
